Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Summary and concrete bounds below; full runbook excerpt and diagram attached. Please let us know which items you want bulleted for your legal SLA appendix and which you want in technical runbook form.

Short answers (numerical targets):
- RPO (data & state): 
  - Model artifacts (weights, checkpoints): near-zero; replicated across regions with asynchronous object-store replication. Typical replication lag under normal conditions: <30s; conservative acceptance for contractual RPO = 60s.
  - Request/session KV (customer session tokens, ephemeral inference session state): our default is best-effort replication; for Dedicated/Private customers we offer active replication with target RPO = 5s (with network link healthy). For Hosted customers, RPO for session state is measured as <60s when using our session persistence feature.
- RTO (recovery time objective): 
  - Control plane and routing: target RTO = 10 minutes (this covers routing policy failover to secondary region and re-establishment of service endpoints).
  - Model serving / inference availability: target RTO = 15-30 minutes depending on model size and cold-start needs (we publish model warm-up profiles in the model catalog).
  - Full service restoration (including KV reconciliation and long-tail cache rehydration): target RTO = 2 hours in extreme scenarios.

Failover sequencing (playbook excerpt):
1) Detect & triage (0-2 minutes): monitoring triggers auto-incident, primary region is marked unhealthy.
2) Control-plane failover (2-10 minutes): Smart routing flips traffic to secondary region based on policy (region priority, latency, and customer pinning). DNS TTLs are preconfigured to 60s or lower for customers requiring rapid failover.
3) Model endpoint activation (5-30 minutes): Secondary region spins the pre-provisioned containers/pods with cached model shards. For models with cold-start risks, we maintain warm standby pools for Dedicated customers to reduce this to ~5 minutes.
4) KV / cache sync (concurrent, 0-120 minutes): prefix/KV caches start rehydration from replicated streams; critical keys prioritized. We provide a reconciliation utility to identify missing tokens and rehydrate on-demand.
5) Validation & degrade modes (10-60 minutes): rollout held until smoke tests pass; non-critical features may remain in degraded mode (e.g., debug traces, verbose logging).

SLA exception language (suggested):
- Scheduled maintenance: planned maintenance windows will be communicated 72 hours in advance; these windows are excluded from uptime calculations.
- Cross-region catastrophic outage: service-level credits apply only if regional redundancy was requested and enabled in the customer's provisioning. Where warm-standby was not selected, restoration timelines are best-effort and not covered by standard uptime credits — this can be negotiated for Dedicated commitments.

Attachments: redwood_recovery_runbook_v2.pdf (extracted excerpt), playbook-diagram.png. I also attached a pre-filled copy of your spreadsheet with the numeric fields filled (arbortech_continuity_qna.xlsx).

If that looks good I can send a short paragraph for your SLA appendix and a separate technical runbook bundle for your infra team.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik — quick internal note on wording and an edge-case:

- The RPO numbers above look solid. For the SLA appendix we should avoid operational terms like "near-zero" and instead put the conservative contractual bounds (e.g., RPO <= 60s for model artifacts; RPO <= 5s for Dedicated session replication).
- We should explicitly call out DNS TTL behavior for customers who cannot accept DNS-based failover (some banks mandate IP-based routing). Suggest adding a short bullet: "If customer requires IP-level failover, Redwood can offer dedicated egress and pre-provisioned network paths under Dedicated contracts."
- Edge-case: If primary region loses write-ordering guarantees (split-brain), we need to clarify how we handle conflicting session tokens. Suggest we add the reconciliation utility's idempotency note and retention windows.

I can help word the SLA paragraph if you want — also note we should not promise 5-minute RTO for all models under Hosted unless warm-standby is purchased.

Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 12:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: ArborTech continuity questionnaire — suggested clarifications

Agree with Ben — a few extra clarifications for legal/ops: 

- Reconciliation & retention: our reconciliation utility has a configurable retention lookback; default 7 days. For customers that need longer retention we recommend Dedicated config with extended replication logs (up to 30 days). Add that as a bullet.
- Canary & staged routing: our smart routing supports staged canary rollouts at region level (weights by percent); during failover we bias traffic to 100% secondary only after smoke tests succeed; this should be included as an operational control in the runbook excerpt.
- Data sovereignty & certification: for EU customers we ensure replica placement in the EU; for ArborTech (US) note that we default to multi-AZ within-region plus cross-region replicas.

I'll draft a single-paragraph SLA-friendly statement and attach it to the runbook PDF before we send back to Elena.

Karthik
